visualChapters.label: Zoom Drag
visualChapters.title: Zoom Drag
visualChapters.description: Keeping the subject in frame while zooming the lens during a slow exposure creates radial blur pulling surrounding light and environment toward the subject — surreal and distorted.

images.description: Experimental portrait created by keeping the subject in the frame while zooming the lens during a slow exposure. The resulting radial blur pulls the surrounding light and environment toward the subject, creating a surreal and distorted feeling.

visualChapters.label: Shutter Drag
visualChapters.title: Shutter Drag
visualChapters.description: Slow shutter speed with intentional camera movement creates motion and blur across the frame. The movement of the camera itself becomes part of the photograph.

images.description: Experimental portrait using slow shutter speed and intentional camera movement, creating motion and blur across the frame.

visualChapters.label: Translucent Screen
visualChapters.title: Behind the Screen
visualChapters.description: A set with a translucent plastic screen and red lighting. Ghostface appearing behind the screen creates an unsettling Halloween atmosphere — creepy without being overly obvious.

images.description: Ghostface appearing behind a translucent plastic screen with red lighting. The figure seems to creep up behind the main subject, creating an unsettling Halloween atmosphere.

visualChapters.label: Spiderweb Set
visualChapters.title: Watched
visualChapters.description: Fake spiderweb set with purple and red lighting. Composition creates an unsettling feeling — almost like spying on the subject from the perspective of a stalker or serial killer.

images.description: Portrait from the fake spiderweb set with purple and red lighting. The composition creates an unsettling feeling, almost as if the subject is being secretly watched.

closingStory: For me, this shoot wasn't just about the photographs. It was the beginning of finding a community where I could experiment, learn, and keep getting better at photography. Since this was my first time meeting the FPC team, the shoot was also a really interesting social experience. I got to network, meet a lot of people with similar interests, and see how other photographers approached the same environment in completely different ways. I went home that day feeling like I'd found a really good photography community. I had experimented with techniques I hadn't really tried before, met a bunch of interesting people, and came away with some photographs that I genuinely loved.
